I advise him to handle business and household arrangements by letter or in person, rather than by telephone, because the latter course would involve him in disputes, and disputes encourage ill feeling.
Sleep indoors. The bedroom is healthy, and the outdoor sleeping porch is exposed to weather and insects. Also, it may be noisy.
I advise him to follow the custom of the majority of the people among whom he lives.
Drink tap water or well water.

I should advise him to own nothing beyond daily use, and to lend anything he has to whoever asks, because owning things beyond daily use involves care, and care involves worry, and worry is undesirable.

I advise him to make short trips on foot or bicycle, because I think walking and cycling are more healthful exercises than riding on a self-balancing motor scooter, and because I do not wish to see people become slaves to any habit.

I advise him to refrain from thanking and praising people for ordinary help, because I think it unwise to encourage in oneself or others a habit of thanking and praising people for what is expected of them. The habit dulls perception of the common and the normal, and tends to make one satisfied with average performance. Also, it seems to me undesirable to habituate people to expect thanks and praise for doing what they ought to do. Thanks and praise are properly reserved for work well and unselfishly done, in circumstances calling for some personal sacrifice.
I advise him to keep sunday free of shopping, because shopping on sunday interferes with family life and public worship, and because it compels shop workers to labor on a day of rest.

I advise him to handle business and household arrangements by telephone, because the majority of people seem to prefer that method, and because I see no reason why he should depart from the customary practice of the society in which he lives.
Advise him to make short trips on foot or by bicycle.

I advise him to shop on Sunday, as on any other day, because, if he does not, he will lose a common day of rest with his family and his congregation, and because the ordinary people, among whom he lives, shop on Sunday.

Advise him to refrain from thanking or praising people for ordinary help. The reasons are: (1) thankfulness for small services is troublesome, and praise is troublesome too; (2) thankfulness and praise are likely to become habit, and habits are undesirable; (3) thankfulness and praise are likely to encourage expectation of them, and that is undesirable; (4) they may encourage vanity in the helped person, and vanity is undesirable.
Advise him to drink mainly filtered or bottled water. Because you have learned that a number of reputable people do so, and because you yourself prefer to do so.

I should advise sleeping indoors in a closed bedroom, because sleeping outdoors in all weathers can hardly benefit health, and may do harm. In winter the pores of the skin are closed, and to expose them to cold may check perspiration and so check the natural elimination of waste matter from the system. In summer, on the other hand, the skin is active, and to keep it active is desirable. Therefore, sleeping in a closed room in summer facilitates perspiration, and so facilitates health. Moreover, a bedroom is warmer in winter and cooler in summer than an outdoor porch.

Advise him to buy a home. The reasons are these: First, he can do so more cheaply than he can rent one. Secondly, he will have a stake in the community, and that stake will grow. Thirdly, he will have a personal interest in keeping the place clean and healthy. Fourthly, he will have an incentive to steady work and so good behaviour.

Advise him to type on the standard keyboard. The reasons are that you cannot foresee whether the rearranged keyboard will become general, and, if it does not, he will have wasted time; and that, if it does become general, he will have to learn two systems instead of one.

Accept an unmarried couple sharing a home before or instead of marriage. First, because the reasons given for doing so are better than any given for not doing so. Second, because you personally have no right to forbid people to live together as they please, provided they do not interfere with other people.

Advise him to wear the same plain clothing as everyone else in his community, because the choice of a personal style of dress is a matter of personal taste, and the taste of the ordinary person is probably as good a guide as any other.

Advise him to choose his own clothes. The reasons are: First, because choosing one's own dress is personal freedom, and personal freedom is good. Secondly, because choosing one's own dress is a mark of self-respect, and self-respect is good. Thirdly, because choosing one's own dress prevents envy and competition, and envy and competition are bad.

I advise you to rent a house, because I think you will enjoy life more if you do not own one. The main reason is that you will be free to move, and so can choose your place of abode according to your tastes and means, and can suit your habits to your income. The additional advantage of not having to think about repairs is worth something; so is the escape from responsibility for insurance. The disadvantages of renting are that you must live in a neighbourhood you do not like, and must put up with inconveniences you would not tolerate in a permanent home of your own choosing. If, however, you prefer disadvantages to independence, buy a house.

Advise him to type on the standard keyboard. The reasons are these: First, you have learned that a number of estimable people have chosen to do so; secondly, you have no information that they are wrong; and, thirdly, you have no information that anybody is under a duty to follow them.

I should advise a person in this situation to buy a home, because I think it is better to be a property owner than a tenant. The sense of possession is pleasant, and the sense of security agreeable. A man feels more at ease in his own house than in a hired one; and he has a personal interest in the maintenance of social order. Moreover, the possession of property helps to make a man thrifty and steady. Finally, by becoming a property owner, he contributes to the strength of the state.

Advise him to type on the standard keyboard. The reasons are these: First, he will learn to type more quickly. Secondly, he will be able to read his notes more easily. Thirdly, he will be able to type matter that is not familiar to him. Fourthly, he will be able to type matter that is familiar to him in a form easier to read. Fifthly, he will be able to type matter that is strange to him in a form easier to read. Sixthly, he will be able to type matter that is both familiar and strange to him in forms easy to read together.

I should advise the person to follow the second course. First, because plain clothing marks no one out, and plain clothes are ugly and unattractive. Secondly, because plain clothes are a bore in wear, and Thirdly, because plain clothes encourage slovenliness.

I advise him to choose his own clothes. First, because plain dressing makes him easy to single out, and so hinders his freedom to express himself. Secondly, because it hinders other people from expressing themselves freely about him.

Advise him to rent a home. First, because a house is cheaper to live in than to own; secondly, because, if he has children, he may wish to move, and an owner must sell at a loss; thirdly, because owning encourages extravagance; and, lastly, because it is undesirable to have too close an interest in a particular spot on earth.

I should advise the person to train on the standard keyboard, because to type on any other would mean waste of time. The standard keyboard is universally used, and learning to type on it involves least waste.

Advise him to wear the same plain clothing as everyone else in his community, unless he has personal reasons for not doing so. The reasons given for plain clothing by those who wear it are not convincing, and the adoption of it by respectable people has probably no further motive than conformity.
Advise him to rent a home. First, because you do not think buying a home is wise for a person in his position. Secondly, because you do not think renting a home is unwise for him.

Advise him to type on the standard keyboard. The reason is that, in the long run, speed on a machine is gained by practice, and practice on one kind of machine is wasted on another. Also, an unfamiliar keyboard introduces confusion.
